result.summary: The new setting is persisted but cannot be edited through the UI and has no effect on shutdown behavior.

findings.title: Connect the new context value to a form input
findings.body: settings.html contains no shutdown_drain_timeout input, so adding this context key renders nothing. Normal browser submissions omit the field and line 550 writes 60.0, including after a direct POST successfully saves 120.5. The existing test_settings_page_renders_new_config_fields assertion also requires this missing input.
findings.recommendation: Add a numeric input associated with settings-form, supporting fractional seconds, and preserve the current value when the field is absent.

findings.title: Apply the saved timeout to the shutdown drain
findings.body: Posting shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 now persists that value, but shutdown still uses _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT at scheduler.py:634. That constant is initialized at import from the environment or 60.0 (lines 58–81) and never reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout. With no environment override, the newly saved 120.5-second setting therefore still allows only 60 seconds for draining, even after restart.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the drain timeout from the current settings at shutdown, applying the environment override explicitly, and test that saving a non-default value changes the actual drain deadline.

next_steps: Complete the template and scheduler integration, then verify browser round-trip persistence and shutdown behavior.
